pages.text: Shellfish firms hope EU export deal will 'lift a burden' Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Shellfish firms hope EU deal will 'lift a burden' 7 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Paul Murphy East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire climate and environment correspondent BBC Jo Ackers, from the Independent Shellfishermen's Co-Operative, says exports currently have to be signed off by a vet Food producers have welcomed a draft deal between the UK and the EU which could remove checks on exports that were put in place after Brexit. The agreement should mean savings for the shellfish industry in Bridlington, East Yorkshire, which exports lobster and crab to France, Spain and Portugal and generates at least £10m for the local economy. Jo Ackers, from the Independent Shellfisherman's Co-operative, said it would "lift a burden" from businesses exporting produce. "All of our exports have needed to be signed off by vets because they are live exports and this involves significant expense and paperwork," she said. The BBC understands a 200-page draft text for a so-called SPS (sanitary and phytosanitary) agreement has been circulated to EU nations in Brussels . Since the UK formally left the EU in January 2020, many food exports have needed extra certificates to confirm the product meets the health requirements of the destination country. pages.text: Shoplifting measures welcomed by Birmingham traders Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Shoplifting measures welcomed by traders 4 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Bob Hockenhull West Midlands Getty Images The government pilot in the West Midlands will focus on prolific offenders Shopkeepers in the West Midlands have welcomed the announcement of new measures to cut shoplifting. The region is one of 16 police force areas chosen as part of a government pilot to target prolific retail offenders, which could see persistent thieves tagged and banned from high streets. Mani Gill, vice-chair of the Soho Road Business Improvement District (BID), Birmingham, said shoplifting was a daily occurrence, with small businesses least able to absorb the costs. Alex Goss, lead for retail crime at the National Police Chief's Council , said he welcomed the pilot to tackle prolific retail crime offenders "who continue to cause harm to businesses, retail workers and local communities". The new measures announced by the Home Secretary on Wednesday will focus on about 500 of the country's most prolific offenders, who the government said were "responsible for a disproportionate amount of shop theft". It said they could face restrictions on their movements including the use of GPS tags, along with being banned from the high street. Check out some questions to ask yourself as you figure out what's best for you. Going back to school can be an exciting endeavor—advancing your education can open new paths in your current career or offer a fresh start to a new career entirely. Whether your reasons for going back to school are personal or professional, several benefits of achieving a higher level of education may help you make your choice. Professional benefits: With a degree, you can explore new jobs, change careers , or advance in your current one. Financial benefits: A higher education level correlates with higher incomes. Signs and Symptoms of Bird Flu in People For Everyone Dec. 20, 2024 Key points Most human cases of bird flu, caused by avian influenza A(H5) virus, in the United States have been mild, so far, and most were in people who had known exposure to sick or infected animals. The severity of illness associated with bird flu has ranged from mild to severe, including death. The reported signs and symptoms of bird flu in humans have varied. Eye redness has been the predominant symptom among recent U.S. cases of avian influenza A(H5) virus infection. Respiratory symptoms and fever were also reported. The possibility of human infections with avian influenza virus that result in severe illness remains and underscores the importance of ongoing prevention and surveillance efforts. It can cause mild to severe illness, and at times can lead to death. Symptoms Flu can cause mild to severe illness, and at times can lead to death. Flu symptoms usually come on suddenly. People who have flu often feel some or all of these signs and symptoms: fever* or feeling feverish/chills cough sore throat runny or stuffy nose muscle or body aches headaches fatigue (tiredness) some people may have vomiting and diarrhea, though this is more common in children than adults. *It's important to note that not everyone with flu will have a fever. Close simon04's Diary DinoData: a phone-first tag editor that explains every tag Posted by simon04 on 4 November 2026 in English . DinoData is a web-based tag editor for OpenStreetMap nodes, ways and relations, designed for phones first. Open an object, see what it is and what each tag means in your language, edit the tags with inputs suited to them, and save as a changeset . Geometry is not edited. It runs entirely in the browser and is hosted on Wikimedia Toolforge. It started as a Wikidata editor; the OpenStreetMap mode lives next to it in the same app. Finding an object Search for a place, or paste what you have: an openstreetmap.org URL (including edit and API URLs), an iD or JOSM remote control link, a short ID like n123 or way 123 , or coordinates. Other text is a place search with Photon and Nominatim . “Near me” lists the tagged objects around you via the Overpass API , handy while surveying. Close simon04's Diary OSM formats compared with TOML Posted by simon04 on 4 November 2026 in English . OSM formats compared with TOML OpenStreetMap data comes in several text formats. OSM XML is exact but verbose, OSM JSON has no comments, and Level0L is easy to type but has no grammar beyond its parser. TOML has comments, a spec and parsers in most languages, including Python’s standard library. So what would OSM data look like as TOML? I came across this question while adding an OSM tag editor to DinoData . Below, each format is compared with TOML using the examples from the OSM wiki, and the TOML versions are checked with Python’s tomllib . Level0L is the text format of the Level0 editor. DinoData reads and writes it in the OSM text view ( src/osm/level0.ts , src/osm/tags.ts ). It looks a bit like TOML : key = value lines, # comments, and headers that start a section. But the two formats are not compatible. This page compares them, together with the other formats DinoData meets, and shows how OSM data could look as TOML. Level0L (lines of text): editing in Level0. pages.text: Six Fish These Small Sound-Emitting Tags Are Helping Save | Smithsonian Voices | Smithsonian Environmental Research Center Smithsonian Magazine Skip to main content Smithsonian Environmental Research Center Six Fish These Small Sound-Emitting Tags Are Helping Save Scientists are tracking animals underwater with “acoustic telemetry” tags—and their discoveries are changing how we protect them Kristen Goodhue November 5, 2026 Get our Newsletter! Get our Newsletter! Dusky shark, Carcharhinus obscurus ( CC-BY-NC-ND-2.0 ) Richard Ling An app tells beachgoers in Massachusetts and Maine if a shark has entered the area. Fishermen in Delaware check their phones to avoid accidentally catching endangered Atlantic sturgeon. Dwindling American shad, once cut off from their spawning grounds by dams, are returning in droves. Each of these stories became possible in part because of tiny “acoustic telemetry” tags and a vast network of researchers deploying them along the East Coast of the U.S. With acoustic telemetry technology, each tag emits a unique, ultrasonic “ping.” Along the Eastern seaboard, thousands of electronic receivers are listening for those pings, ready to detect any tagged animal that swims within about half a kilometer. Researchers in the Atlantic Cooperative Telemetry Network , or “ACT” for short, have been tagging animals for over two decades. Now managed by the Smithsonian Environmental Research Center , the network unites scientists from over 120 organizations from Maine to North Carolina. The document is tailored to the smallest of businesses — those with no employees other than the owner, or "non-employer" firms as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration. These firms are also often colloquially referred to as "solopreneurs." While written for non-employer firms, the information in this document will also be useful to businesses with very few employees or with minimal IT infrastructure. The goal is to introduce the fundamentals of a small business cybersecurity program in non-technical language to set a solid cybersecurity risk management foundation. Considerations for maturing cybersecurity risk management as the business scales are included, which also makes the document useful for entities of varying sizes. Established through a Memorandum of Agreement between U.S. Department of Energy and the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) in August 2026 , the SBIC-E Initiative combines DOE’s scientific, technical, and commercialization expertise with SBA’s long-established Small Business Investment Company (SBIC) Program. Through DOE’s Office of Technology Commercialization (OTC), the Department will identify strategic technology priorities, provide technical and commercialization expertise, and help engage the investment community. The SBA Office of Investment and Innovation will administer the initiative and encourage the formation and growth of investment funds focused on those priorities. During the Great Depression, the roadway helped migrants find their way to new jobs in the West. During World War II, it facilitated the transportation of munitions and armaments en route to the Pacific theater. Later, it became a busy thoroughfare for Americans wanting to explore their country. Storefronts, towns, gas stations, cafes and much more grew up along its edges. Then, as major interstates became the main byways for traveling Americans, Route 66 fell into obsolescence, becoming more a time capsule than roadway. January 17, 2024 Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) What to know Social determinants of health (SDOH) are the nonmedical factors that influence health outcomes. They are the conditions in which people are born, grow, work, live, worship, and age. These conditions include a wide set of forces and systems that shape daily life such as economic policies and systems, development agendas, social norms, social policies, and political systems. CDC has adapted this definition from the World Health Organization. Why are SDOH important to CDC? SDOH are one of three priority areas for Healthy People 2030 , along with health equity and health literacy. Healthy People 2030 sets data-driven national objectives in five key areas of SDOH : healthcare access and quality, education access and quality, social and community context, economic stability, and neighborhood and built environment. Some examples of SDOH included in Healthy People 2030 are safe housing, transportation, and neighborhoods; polluted air and water; and access to nutritious foods and physical health opportunities. pages.text: Sociology Standards Sociology Standards Skip Navigation Sociology Standards The U.S. Census Bureau’s Statistics in Schools (SIS) activities are based on relevant education standards and guidelines that outline the foundational knowledge and skills students should have at certain levels. The SIS activities — which are designed to supplement or guide, not replace, existing curricula — help develop these skills and knowledge. Not all educators use the same standards. For this reason, many of the activities address multiple standards and guidelines. SOCIOLOGY American Sociological Association’s National Standards for High School Sociology Published in 2015, these standards are designed to assist teachers and administrators who want to develop high-quality, developmentally appropriate introductory sociology courses over one semester for students in ninth through 12th grades. These standards are organized by four learning domains; each represents a broad area of sociological knowledge and study appropriate for high school.
